note: A-F21 floor-settling test. Tier-A floor (pooled-mean fit, decoys 0.15/0.25/0.35) vs window length, one 62s capture, offline nested-window fits. df=0.05Hz -> A-F21 minimum 2/df=40s = 2 resolution cells.
reading_floor: Floor falls 3.28e-5 (1 cell) -> 2.64e-5 (2 cells/40s) then FLATTENS (2.5-2.8e-5). Settles at exactly 2/df=40s, confirming A-F21's resolution explanation (below 2 cells, signal leaks into the null and biases the floor high).
reading_selfcheck: With a 62s full window the 70% sub-window (43.6s) clears 2 cells, so the self-check ratio is 0.94 (clean ~1.0). At GELB's 49.5s full window the 70% sub-window is 34.6s=1.73 cells (<2), so its floor is inflated by its OWN resolution, giving ratio 1.47 — not a falling floor. REFINEMENT: full window must be >= 2/(0.7*df) ~= 57s so the self-check's sub-window itself clears 2 cells.
note_absolute_floor: PINK's plateau floor ~2.6e-5 vs GELB's converged 1e-5 — same order, both far under the 0.0005 bound (19-50x); the ~2.6x gap is plausibly PINK's more-inclusive stage-minus-svg mask (200k vs 178k px); per-element sign-hide on the tip should tighten it. The reproducible result is the SHAPE (settles at 2 cells), not the absolute.
